Shelves, not folders

A collection gathers different kinds without moving or copying them. Drive the press once: assemble a shelf, slide the kind lens across it, then remove one membership without touching the entity.

ordered contains many shelves per entity one kind per list lens

01One shelf, many kinds

A collection is an entity whose outgoing contains edges carry the reading order. The shelf below receives a task, two docs, a session, and a teammate. Then the product’s kind list becomes a lens: Tasks shows the task; Docs shows the docs.

02Two ways to nest collections

Both shapes are real, but they answer different questions. Use hierarchy to subdivide one collection tree. Use contains when one curated shelf should include another collection as an item.

A

Subdivision

Collections may be parent and child because hierarchy is homogeneous: both ends are collections in the same Space.

Northlake guidesparent collection
Setupchild collection
Graphchild collection
B

Curation

A collection may contain another collection because contains accepts any entity kind as its destination.

Release deskcollection
contains
Field notesmember collection

Boundary. A collection cannot contain itself. Because contains is not acyclic, avoid circular curation between different collections.

03Remove a membership, not the entity

One doc can sit on several shelves at once. Remove it from Release notes and watch what does not move: the doc stays in the graph, and the other two contains edges stay intact.

CLI shape behind the demonstration

tm8 collection add <collection-id> <entity-id> [--position <number>]

Leave out --position to append after the current maximum. Re-adding an existing member repositions its one edge; it does not duplicate it.

tm8 collection remove <collection-id> <entity-id> --yes

Removal deletes the matching contains edge. The entity is untouched.

no copies, it's a graph.
